newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: U.N. aid official wounded in Sierra Leone ambush.
newsitem.headline: U.N. aid official wounded in Sierra Leone ambush.

text.p: Unidentified gunmen shot and wounded a senior U.N. aid official in Sierra Leone and fatally wounded his driver in an ambush on the road from the northern town of Makeni to the capital Freetown, U.N. sources said.
Robert Painter, the American head of the U.N. Department of Humanitarian Affairs in the West African nation, was shot in the foot in the ambush late on Tuesday, one source told Reuters.
The driver, a Sierra Leonian aged 53, died later in hospital, the sources added.

Around six attackers, some bare-chested, some in combat fatigues or wearing bandanas, sprayed a convoy of two vehicles with automatic arms fire near a village called Madina, 15 miles (25 km) from Makeni and about 90 miles (145 km) from Freetown.

The attack was the first time a U.N. vehicle has been specifically targeted. The road had been safe since before President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah and rebel leader Foday Sankoh signed a peace deal in November.

"If, as it appears, this was a deliberate ambush on clearly marked U.N. and NGO (Non Governmental Organisation) vehicles, it could have serious implications for the delivery of humanitarian assistance in Sierra Leone," a U.N. spokesperson said.
The motive and identity of the attackers was not immediately clear.

Fighting between the army and the rebels, who took up arms in 1991, has largely ceased but implementation of the deal has dragged and clashes between the army and traditional hunters, their former allies, have complicated peace efforts.
Painter and other officials had been visits projects in Makeni. Kathy Jones, British deputy head of the U.N. peace operation in Sierra Leone, and a World Bank official were also in the car.
